reasons: No test is visible in the packet.
Handles missing text and missing quotes without crashing.

terms.meaning: A reusable piece of the screen that is drawn from data passed into it.
A web address ending that tells a browser to scroll to and highlight a phrase on a page.
A pattern used to search text, here allowing flexible spacing and capital letters.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Icons and link builder imports
sections.what: Brings in the icons and the function that builds jump links.
sections.why: The panel needs these to draw badges and build the link to the live page.

sections.name: SourceValidation
sections.title: Shape of a validation record
sections.what: Describes the fields a validation record carries, including the quote, page address, captured text, and match and snapshot flags.
sections.why: Defines the data the panel expects.
sections.watch_out: Many fields are optional and may be empty, so code that reads them must handle missing values.

sections.name: pickValidation
sections.title: Choosing the best example
sections.what: From a list of records, picks the strongest one: an exact match with a matched snapshot and image is preferred, then weaker options. Returns nothing when no record is complete.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows the most convincing evidence first.
sections.watch_out: The order of preference decides which evidence users see, so changing it changes what they are shown.

sections.name: locate
sections.title: Finding the quote in the text
sections.what: Looks for the exact quote first. If that fails, it looks for the same words with any spacing and capital letters. Returns the start and end positions, or nothing.
sections.why: Likely reason: captured text can differ slightly in spacing, so a loose match still finds the quote.
sections.watch_out: The highlight can appear even when the badge says the quote was not exactly re-located, because the two use different checks.

sections.name: CapturedPassage
sections.title: Panel that shows the passage
sections.what: Draws the badge for exact or not exact match, the passage with the highlight, the link to the live page, and the snapshot status.
sections.why: Likely reason: tells users clearly how strong the match is.
sections.watch_out: Read the badge and the highlight together; they are not the same check.

summary: Shows the saved source passage for one citation, with the cited quote highlighted and a link to jump to it on the live web page.
purpose: Lets a reviewer check that the quoted words really come from the captured source text.
why: Likely reason: makes the match status explicit, so a reader does not assume a quote is verified when it is not.
how: Takes one validation record, looks for the quote inside the stored captured text, highlights the match if found, then shows a match badge, the scrollable text, a jump link and the snapshot status.
inputs: One source validation record with the quote, captured text, page address, publisher, capture date and match flags.
outputs: A panel with a match badge, the passage text with the quote highlighted, a link to the live page and a snapshot status note.
risks: If the quote is not found, the full text is shown with no highlight. The badge and the highlight come from different checks and can disagree.
debug: If the text is missing, the panel says no captured text is stored, so check the stored captured text. If the highlight is wrong, check the locate step and the quote value. If the jump link is missing, check the page address.
